basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 19.' and it opens 'Vers. 19. Sodomam et Gomorrham. Istae civitates notae sunt interitu suae subversionis.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 19. Sodomam et Gomorrham. Istae civitates notae sunt interitu suae subversionis. Samariten. A quo Samaria, quae sic vocatur et Assyriis et Hebraeis. | Dicta est autem Antiochia vel Epiphania. Amathaeum. Haec nomina ignorantur, vel quia deletae sunt istae gentes bello Aethiopico, vel quia ignoratur quae nomina nunc habeant
